items.rationale: The washing-machine leak qualifies as escape of water under §2.4.2. Section 7.1.7(h) covers necessary residue removal from the affected utility-room floor; €65 allows for a small cleaning job.
The adjoining hallway was also reached by the escaping water. Section 7.1.7(h) covers necessary cleaning of its affected floor, estimated at €80 gross.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers checking the appliance and connections to confirm the source no longer leaks, even if the machine itself is not insured. Allow €85 for the inspection, not appliance repair.
Section 7.1.7(a) covers dismantling and disposing of affected fixed trim. Allow €95 gross for removal and disposal of the damaged lengths.
Fixed skirting is a building component under §4.2.2. Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.9 limit the €240 allowance to supply and fitting of equivalent trim in the affected areas.

items.description: Undamaged upstairs bedroom cleaning and repainting
items.rationale: Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude work in the separate bedroom because it sustained no documented physical damage from the leak.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary moisture measurements in both affected rooms. Allow €170 gross, consistent with the comparable floor and wall-base survey in Case 21.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying in the two affected rooms. Allow €105 for drying services distinct from equipment rental and separately billed labour; §7.1.8(c) bars duplication.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers necessary drying-equipment hire. Allow €55 gross for the unit, provided its hire is not already included in the drying charge.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour at customary rates; four hours at €48 gross gives €192. Section 7.1.8(c) excludes any hours already included in the measurement or drying charges.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) exclude drying and related measurements in a separate room with no documented damage from the leak.

items.description: Transport of affected painting to specialist
items.rationale: Section 5.2.6 covers specialist transport but gives restoration first call on the shared €1,190 gross cap. An estimated €100 for transport is payable only if restoration leaves enough room for it, with transport first in invoice order for that balance.
Section 5.2.6 covers the professional assessment only from the cap remaining after restoration and then transport. If a balance reaches this line, estimate €120 gross, limited to that balance.

items.description: Drying and stabilisation of affected painting
items.rationale: Section 5.2.6 covers conservation drying and stabilisation, but this line receives only the balance left after restoration, transport and assessment. If a balance remains, estimate €140 gross.

items.description: Full restoration of affected hallway painting
items.rationale: Under §5.2.6, restoration is applied first against the single cap for the unscheduled painting. Full specialist restoration is estimated to reach the €1,000 net cap, or €1,190 gross at 19% VAT if incurred under §7.7.
Section 5.2.6 applies only to an item affected by the insured event. The second painting was unaffected, so it receives no separate conservation allowance.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes separate administrative and processing fees, and §5.2.6 does not list them as covered conservation costs.
